THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1. Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 29.09.2018 passed in MVC No.7423/2016 by the Court of Additional Small causes Judge and the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Bengaluru (for short 'the Tribunal'), the respondent No.1 therein has preferred this appeal.

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that on 18.07.2016 at about 7.00 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding in a motor bike bearing Registration No. KA 05 EF 9088 as a Pillion rider on Thangachaguppe Road near Vinpack Biscuit factory.
At that time a goods vehicle came and dashed against the motor bike causing grievous injuries to the petitioner.
Hence, a police complaint was lodged regarding the same.

However, the number of the vehicle which caused the accident was not noted by the petitioner or the rider of the motor bike at the time of the accident and hence the number of the vehicle involved in the accident was not mentioned in the complaint given to the police.
The complaint was lodged stating that it was a hit and run case and there was a request made to the police to find out the number of the offending vehicle.

Subsequently, after verifying the number of the vehicle from the CCTV Cameras present in the locality and also after enquiry made from few persons, who were present at the spot the petitioner came to know about the involvement of the goods vehicle bearing Registration No. KA 05 AF 0183.
The same happened to be a de-max Isuzu goods vehicle.

However,
in the complaint lodged to the police it was stated that luggage goods auto had dashed against the motor bike.

Thereafter, the petitioner preferred MVC No.7423/2016 against the owner of the vehicle bearing registration No. KA 05 AF 0183 (de-max Isuzu vehicle) and the insurance Company which had duly insured the said vehicle.
The tribunal believing the version of the petitioner has awarded a compensation of Rs.11,05,253/- to be paid along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.

5. On the ground that the said de-max isuzu vehicle bearing registration No. KA 05 AF 0183 was not involved in the accident and the tribunal erred in holding so, the present appeal is filed by the insurance company.
It is also contended that the compensation awarded is excessive.

6. The main ground relied upon by the insurance company is that at the time of giving the complaint it is alleged that the vehicle involved in the accident is a goods auto vehicle and de-max isuzu vehicle is a much bigger vehicle and belongs to a different class altogether and the complainant could not have confused a goods auto with de-max isuzu vehicle and the present vehicle is implicated with an ulterior motive on making illegal gains and that the vehicle which has been involved in the accident is not properly proved by the petitioners before the tribunal.

7. The petitioner to establish that de-max isuzu vehicle bearing registration No. KA 05 AF 0183 was involved in the accident has stated in his evidence that he could not note down the number of the vehicle immediately at the time of the accident but subsequently it was verified through CCTV and upon enquiry with the people present at the spot where accident took place, they came to know that the accident was caused by de-max isuzu vehicle bearing registration No. KA 05 AF 0183.
His evidence has not been impeached to the cross- examination.

Furthermore, to corroborate the evidence given by the petitioner the police after investigation have filed a charge-sheet against the driver of the de-max isuzu vehicle bearing registration No. KA 05 AF 0183 and the owner of the vehicle has not denied the involvement of the vehicle and the accident at any point of time.
He has infact remained ex-parte before the tribunal.
8. It can't be presumed that the police have colluded both the petitioner and have filed a false charge-sheet unless the respondent adduces some evidence in this regard.
Given the facts and circumstances of the case, one has to conclude that vehicle bearing registration No. KA 05 AF 0183 which happens to be a de-max isuzu vehicle was involved in the accident.
I find no error in the decision of the tribunal insofar as it relates to this accept is concerned.
9. In respect of the compensation awarded the case of the appellant is that the petitioner has not sustained any functional disability and there is no loss of income.
The petitioner has fairly stated due to the injury sustained is unable to carry out the work that he was previously doing and his evidence has not been impeached in this regard.

Based on the evidence let in the tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.11,05,253/- to the petitioners out of which Rs.4,27,680/- has been awarded in respect of loss of future earning due to disability.
The insurance company has failed to adduce any cogent reasons as to why the decision of the tribunal has to be interfered with.
10. For the aforementioned reasons, the appeal being devoid of merits is hereby dismissed.
